The statement is candid about a severe negative shock from COVID-19, which will weigh on output and raise downside risks; however, relative to a purely macro read, the tone is partly offset by decisive policy. Consistent with the credit channel and financial accelerator literature (e.g., Bernanke–Gertler; Oliner and Rudebusch; Gertler and Gilchrist), the FOMC’s rapid move to the effective lower bound, large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, expanded repo operations, discount window and liquidity-buffer measures, and dollar swap lines should help stabilize funding markets and sustain the flow of credit, dampening the downturn’s amplification through balance sheets. With market- and survey-based inflation expectations little changed, the inflation-forecast-targeting perspective (Svensson; Svensson and Woodford) implies that credibility, QE, and ongoing monitoring can support a return toward the 2 percent objective even at the zero lower bound, reducing deflation risk highlighted by liquidity-trap concerns. Net sentiment remains negative due to the immediate growth hit, but policy actions warrant a less negative assessment than before.
